learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected Nowhere and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Opened membrane from equal 1 L volumes and 10 versus 30 sugar dots. Water volumes became 0.50 and 1.50 L, both concentration 0.20 mol/L. Moved ten sugar left: 20 each and 1 L each. Again left: 30 versus 10 and 1.50 versus 0.50 L. Moved right restored equal amounts and volumes.
observations.reveal: Corrected to left to right for original setup, referenced initial equilibrium, explained water toward higher sugar concentration and named osmosis. Stated raised-level pressure is ignored.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshots inspected. Dotted pink membrane, sugar dots and unequal water levels visible. Equal final setup showed equal concentrations but a rightward water arrow remained, apparently the latest movement indication without explicit history label. All reveal text readable.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviews inspected.

prediction.reason: Clear selective-permeability premise supports a directional commitment.
prediction.evidence: Water allowed, sugar blocked, nowhere selected.

interaction.reason: Changing sugar distribution reverses volume response and supports equal case.
interaction.evidence: 10/30, 20/20 and 30/10 dots tested with linked volumes.

payoff.reason: Reveal explains the original flow and names the mechanism with pressure caveat.
payoff.evidence: Water concentration difference and ignored level pressure.

clarity.reason: Quantities are clear but sugar-transfer control semantics and residual flow arrow can confuse.
clarity.evidence: Sugar cannot cross beside move-sugar arrows; equal concentrations still rightward arrow.

transfer.reason: Osmosis is generalized within the same apparatus without a new application.
transfer.evidence: Net water flow through membrane defined.

accessibility.evidence: Text volumes and concentrations available; screen reader, keyboard, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.evidence: Initial right volume rises to 1.50 L.

visualExplanation.reason: Dot counts, levels and concentration metrics expose equalization.
visualExplanation.evidence: Both sides reach 0.20 mol/L with unequal volumes.

practicalValue.reason: Introduces a common biological transport principle.

depth.reason: Separates solute amount, volume and concentration.
depth.evidence: 20/20 gives equal volume; 30/10 gives unequal volume at equal concentration.

complexity.reason: Simple controls require concentration and selective-membrane reasoning.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish sugar amount from concentration and infer water movement through selective barrier.
complexity.interfaceBurden: Open button and two constrained redistribution buttons.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Membrane selectivity and osmosis introduced; mol/L not fully explained.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Litres, dot-to-mole mapping and decimal mol/L.

whyCool: Water redistributes even though the visible sugar particles cannot pass the membrane.
caveat: Redistributing sugar is an external setup manipulation but not explicitly labeled as such; water arrow remains at equal final concentrations.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
